title: Comparison of ordinary invertible modules with line modules on a scheme small etale site
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{et}}}(u:U\to X)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. For an ordinary invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], let $A_X(L)=L_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the associated sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], with its sectionwise $\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{et}}}$-module action; for a module morphism $h:L\to K$, let $A_X(h)_u=\Gamma(U,u^*h)$, where module pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback]. A line module on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{et}}}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which becomes isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{et}}}$ on the localized sites of some jointly surjective etale family $U_a\to X$. The functor $A_X$ is an equivalence from ordinary invertible modules, with all module morphisms, to these line modules, with all module morphisms. In particular, every line module is isomorphic to $A_X(L)$ for an ordinary invertible $L$, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(L,K)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{et}}}}(A_X(L),A_X(K))$ is bijective. There is a natural identification $A_X(\mathcal O_X)\simeq\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{et}}}$. For every etale map $v:Y\to X$ there are natural isomorphisms $A_X(L)|_{Y_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq A_Y(v^*L)$, where the restriction evaluates at $w:W\to Y$ by the composite $v\circ w$; these identify $A_X(h)|_{Y_{\mathrm{et}}}$ with $A_Y(v^*h)$ and are compatible with identity maps and composition of etale maps.

source.place: Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), part (2); Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties), finite local freeness, specialized to rank one; Tag 03LC (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial), part (1), for pullback compatibility. The equivalence is restricted to invertible modules.

proof.text: For invertible $L$, quasi-coherence is part of [def-sc-invertible-module], so [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent] supplies the sheaf underlying $A_X(L)$. Its restrictions are semilinear and compose by [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]; thus its sectionwise scalar action makes it a module sheaf. For $h:L\to K$, naturality of the pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] gives $g^*(u^*h(s))=g^*u^*h(g^*s)$, and naturality of the composition comparison in [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $\rho_g(u^*h(s))=u'^*h(\rho_g(s))$. Therefore the stated components define $A_X(h)$. Pullback and global sections preserve identities and compositions, proving the functor laws. For the structure module, $u^*\mathcal O_X\simeq\mathcal O_U$ is the tensor map $a\otimes b\mapsto a\,u^\sharp(b)$ with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. It identifies the restrictions with the ring restrictions, proving $A_X(\mathcal O_X)\simeq\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{et}}}$, including its module action.

proof.text: For etale $v:Y\to X$ and $w:W\to Y$, the component of the restriction comparison is $\Gamma(W,(v\circ w)^*L)\simeq\Gamma(W,w^*v^*L)$ from [def-pc-module-pullback]. The composition is etale: apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition] to the covering $\{v,\mathrm{id}_X\}$ and, over its $Y$ member, $\{w,\mathrm{id}_Y\}$ (use the identity covering over its $X$ member). Compatibility with restrictions and with $h$ follows from the unit-normalized composition comparison of [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]. Explicitly its tensor formula multiplies the intermediate scalar into the final scalar; the inverse inserts $1$ in the intermediate factor. For three successive pullbacks, both composites on local tensor generators multiply the three scalars in their original order, so associativity makes them equal; identity comparisons insert or remove $1$. Since tensor generators locally generate the pullback sheaves, these are equalities of the module maps. This proves the identity, composition and morphism compatibilities claimed in the item.

proof.text: Choose a Zariski trivializing cover $V_i\subseteq X$ for $L$, using [def-sc-invertible-module]. These are objects and a covering of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites]. Pullback along an open immersion is restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], so $L|_{V_i}\simeq\mathcal O_{V_i}$ identifies $v_i^*L$ with the structure module. Step 2 and the structure comparison of Step 1 now identify $A_X(L)$ on each $(V_i)_{\mathrm{et}}$ with its structure module. Thus the functor takes values in the stated line modules.

source.place: Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), proof specialized to locally free rank one modules; Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties), finite local freeness.

proof.text: Given a module-sheaf map $\alpha:A_X(L)\to A_X(K)$, evaluate it on every open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$. Via the natural, unit-compatible restriction identification in [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], these components are $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear maps $L(V)\to K(V)$ commuting with restriction to smaller opens. They therefore define an ordinary module map $h:L\to K$, by the definition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a general etale $u:U\to X$, cover $X$ by opens $V_i$ with frames $e_i$ of $L$ and cover $U$ by $U_i=U\times_XV_i$. The first cover is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites]; its pullback is a cover by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). Naturality of $\alpha$ along $U_i\to V_i$ gives $\alpha_{U_i}(u^*e_i)=u^*(h(e_i))$ using Step 2. Every section on $U_i$ is $b\,u^*e_i$, so linearity gives $\alpha_{U_i}=\Gamma(U_i,u^*h)$. For any $s\in A_X(L)(U)$ the two images in $A_X(K)(U)$ agree on all $U_i$, and hence agree by separatedness. Thus $\alpha=A_X(h)$. Evaluation on opens also shows that $A_X(h)=A_X(h')$ implies $h=h'$, proving the Hom bijection for all module morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), proof specialized to locally free rank one modules; Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties), finite local freeness.

proof.text: Let $G$ be a line module and choose its trivializing etale family $u_a:U_a\to X$ and frames $t_a:\mathcal O_{(U_a)_{\mathrm{et}}}\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_{(U_a)_{\mathrm{et}}}$. Put $R_{ab}=U_a\times_XU_b$. These are objects of the site by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On its localized site set $\beta_{ab}=t_a^{-1}t_b$. A module endomorphism $\beta$ of this structure sheaf is multiplication by its value $g=\beta_{R_{ab}}(1)$: for $q:W\to R_{ab}$, naturality gives $\beta_W(1)=q^\sharp(g)$, and linearity gives $\beta_W(b)=bq^\sharp(g)$. Applying this to the inverse makes $g_{ab}=\beta_{ab}(1)$ a unit. On triple products the identity $(t_a^{-1}t_b)(t_b^{-1}t_c)=t_a^{-1}t_c$ evaluated at $1$ gives $g_{ab}g_{bc}=g_{ac}$, with the functions pulled back to the triple product. On the diagonal it gives $g_{aa}=1$ after diagonal pullback. Thus multiplication by $g_{ab}$ gives ordinary module gluing maps $\mathcal O_{U_b}|_{R_{ab}}\to\mathcal O_{U_a}|_{R_{ab}}$ satisfying exactly the descent cocycle. Here pullbacks of the structure modules use the tensor unit comparison of Step 1. This is a calculation in frames, requiring no general theorem identifying the two categories of modules.

source.place: Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), proof specialized to locally free rank one modules; Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties), finite local freeness.

proof.text: The jointly surjective etale family $(u_a)_a$ is fpqc by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]. Apply the invertible-module descent assertion (3) of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] to the ordinary structure modules $\mathcal O_{U_a}$ and the gluing maps of Step 5. It supplies an ordinary invertible module $L$ and isomorphisms $\lambda_a:u_a^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{U_a}$ compatible with those maps. With our orientation this compatibility reads $\lambda_a=g_{ab}\lambda_b$ on $R_{ab}$ after the canonical pullback comparisons. Consequently $t_aA(\lambda_a)=t_bA(\lambda_b)$ there, because $t_b=t_a\,g_{ab}$. Steps 1 and 2 identify the domains of these local maps with $A_X(L)$ restricted to $R_{ab}$. All covers here are arbitrary set-indexed covers in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; no quasi-compactness or separatedness of $X$ was imposed.

source.place: Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), proof specialized to locally free rank one modules; Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties), finite local freeness.

proof.text: Write $e_a=t_aA(\lambda_a)$. For an object $W\to X$ and $s\in A_X(L)(W)$, restrict to $W_a=W\times_XU_a$ and apply $e_a$ to obtain $r_a\in G(W_a)$. The family $(W_a\to W)_a$ is a covering by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), and Step 6 makes $r_a$ agree on $W_a\times_WW_b$. Its sheaf equalizer axiom therefore gives a unique $r\in G(W)$; define $e_W(s)=r$. Restriction along $W'\to W$, addition and multiplication by $b\in\mathcal O(W)$ commute with this rule because both resulting sections have the same restrictions to all $W'_a$ or $W_a$. Hence $e$ is a module-sheaf map. The inverses $e_a^{-1}$ agree on overlaps as well; the identical gluing rule constructs its inverse. Their composites are identities since they are identities on each $W_a$ and sections are separated. Thus $G\simeq A_X(L)$, proving essential surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), proof specialized to locally free rank one modules; Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties), finite local freeness.

proof.text: Finally choose for each line module $G$ a pair $(L_G,e_G:A_X(L_G)\xrightarrow{\sim}G)$ from Steps 6 and 7. For $f:G\to H$, define its inverse-functor image as the unique ordinary module map with $A_X$-image $e_H^{-1}fe_G$, using Step 4. Uniqueness gives the identity and composition laws. The maps $e_G$ form a natural counit isomorphism. For ordinary $L$, lift $e_{A_X(L)}$ by the same Hom bijection to $L_{A_X(L)}\to L$; lifting its inverse proves this is an isomorphism. Its naturality and the triangle identities follow by applying the faithful $A_X$ and cancelling the $e_G$. This gives an equivalence with the specified functor $A_X$. Steps 1 and 2 already provide its natural structure-module and etale-restriction identifications.
